full_judgment:
Zinat Ara J: In this application under Article 102(2)(a)(ii) of the Constitution, the petitioner called in question the legality of the order dated 10-9-2001 issued by the Deputy Director, Bangladesh Bank (respondent No. 3) under Memo No. Boi Mu Ni (Aba)144/10/ 2001-2250 cancelling Money Changer Licence of the petitioner. 

 3. The petitioner is the Proprietor of James Money Changer having Licence No. Boi Mu Ni (Aba)144/97-862 dated 15-6-1997 granted by Bangladesh Bank (shortly, the Bank) under the Provision of section 3 of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1947. The said business of the petitioner is guided by the directives and conditions affixed by the Bank vide its FF. Circular No. 2 dated 14-1-2001. The petitioner has been carrying on his business with reputation since 1997. The Bank by its memo No. Boi Mu Pabi-30/2001/358 dated 13-3-2001 had informed the petitioner about the inspection of its business by a visiting team of the Bank Thereafter, an inspection was conducted by the said team. The Bank on 28-3-2001 again sent an inspection team by its letter No. Boi Mu Pabi-30/2001-468. The petitioner by his letter dated 20-4-2001 informed to the General Manager. Exchange Policy Division, Bangladesh Bank about receiving the FE Circular No. 18 of 2000 on 20-4-2001 containing a direction of not to issue above two hundred US dollars to any foreign going passenger prior to obtaining visa. Subsequently, the authority on 6th August, 2001 issued another FE Circular No. 19 cancelling FE Circular No. 18/2000 forthwith on and from 6th August, 2001 and all concerned were directed to follow the-guidelines stipulated in FE Circular No. 19. The Bank on 23-6-2001 issued a notice informing the petitioner that the inspection team of the Bank, during its inspection on 13-3-2001 found some irregularities about non-mentioning of rate in buying and selling of foreign currency, violation of FE Circular No. 18 in selling dollars and in not preserving the copies of Biman travel ticket of foreign-going passengers. The petitioner was also asked to show cause within 7 days as to why his licence should not be cancelled for the above irregularities. The petitioner on 30-6-2001 replied to the said show cause notice denying the allegations brought against him. Another inspection team was also sent by the Bank to the petitioner's office on 6-8-2001 and the said inspection was conducted with the fullest satisfaction of the Bank. However, on the basis of the first inspection conducted on 13-3-2001, the Bank cancelled the licence of the petitioner by the impugned letter dated 10-9-2001. 

 12. The moot question to be decided in this Rule is, whether the impugned letter No. Boi Mu Ni (Aba) 144/10/2001-2250 dated 10-9-2001 issued by the Bank cancelling the Money Changer Licence of the petitioner is in accordance with law.
